registration_statements: BTXA has been used clinically for more than half a century. In recent years, patients with upper motor neuron syndrome have been administered BTXA, which has shown good effects, but the optimal dose and concentration as well as standardized recommendations have not been established (Baricich et al., 2008; Wang and Gao, 2008). Currently, only a few countries, including Great Britain, China, and the United States, produce BTXA preparations (Béseler et al., 2012). In China, only the Lanzhou Institute of Biological Products is licensed to produce BTXA. The name of this product is HengLi, and each bottle contains 100 U. BTXA was officially registered for commercial use in the United States in 1989 under the trade name Botox (Wang and Gao, 2008). Although BTXA is a toxic substance, it has been clinically used safely for 50 years in humans (Cigna et al., 2014; Schramm et al., 2014).
